REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
AGENDA
Tuesday, August 03, 2021 - 05:00 p.m.
LOMITA CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
24300 Narbonne Avenue, Lomita, CA 90717
Published by the Office of the City Clerk
VARIOUS TELECONFERENCE LOCATIONS
PURSUANT TO EXECUTIVE ORDER N-08-21 ISSUED BY GOVERNOR NEWSOM, THE PUBLIC AND COUNCIL MAY PARTICIPATE IN THIS MEETING VIA TELECONFERENCE. ALL VOTES TAKEN DURING THIS MEETING WILL BE BY ROLL CALL VOTE, AND THE VOTE WILL BE PUBLICLY REPORTED.
The public may participate in the meeting via a computer or smart device by logging into ZOOM at the following link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82252104971
You may enter your name when prompted do so. If you wish to provide public comment at either the beginning of the meeting or for a particular item, you may either (a) contact the City Clerk's Office before the meeting and provide your name or (b) utilize the "raise hand" option located under the participant's name. Once you click on this option you will be in the rotation to make a public comment.
Please note, if you do not have the audio feature on your device you will need to call (669) 900-6833 and enter ZOOM Meeting ID: 822 5210 4971 then press pound (#). When prompted to enter the participation ID number press pound (#) again. To make a public comment enter "*9". The Clerk's office will be notified, and you will be announced to make a public comment.
Written materials distributed to the City Council within 72 hours of the City Council meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution via the City of Lomita website or by contacting the Deputy City Clerk at l.abbott@lomitacity.com.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, you should contact the office of the City Clerk at (310) 325-7110 (voice) or the California Relay Service. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility to this meeting.
This meeting will be conducted in compliance with CDC guidelines and applicable orders of the Los Angeles County Health Officer.

1  OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

  b. Flag Salute

3. PRESENTATIONS
  Brandon Kamada gave a PowerPoint presentation outlining his Eagle Scout p@ect, the City
  of Lomita Military Banner Program, in partnership with the City of Lomita and the Lomita-
  Harbor City Kiwanis Club as well as the Lomita VFW. The program is proposed to be an
  annual solicitation for recognition banners and will feature active military and veterans who
  have a connection to Lomita. There was some brief discussion regarding the application
  process, length of time banners should be displayed and other logistics. The City Council
  expressed thanks to Brandon for bringing this program forward and suggested he work with
  the VFW to identify local veterans to be recognized as part of the program.

  Mayor Waronek presented Heidi Butzine, PresidenVCEO of the Lomita Chamber of
  Commerce, wilh a 2021 Lemonade Day Proclamation.

  Ms. Butzine spoke of the entrepreneurial efforts of the children who will set up lemonade
  stands in Lomita on Lemonade Day. She thanked City staff, event sponsors, and mentors on
  the volunteer Lemon Council. The kickoff for the event is Saturday, August 7, 2021, at
  9:00 a.m. in front of City Hall.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

9. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION TO APPROVE VESTING TENTATIVE PARCEL
  MAP NO. 83029 TO SUBDIVIDE A 23,2OO SQUARE-FOOT SINGLE-FAMILY
  RESIDENTIAL LOT INTO THREE NEW SINGLE-FAMILY LOTS

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution 2021-28, approving Vesting Tentative Parcel
  Map No. 83029 to subdivide a 23,200 square-foot single-family residential lot into three new
  single-family lots and the conesponding CEQA Categorical Exemption, subject to the
  conditions of approval.
  Associate Planner MacMonan presented the staff report as per the agenda material. She
  stated that neighbors' concerns had been addressed since the Planning Commission meeting
  at which this project had been initially discussed.

  Mayor Pro Tem Segawa opened the public hearing at 6:30 p.m.

  Mayor Waronek returned to the Zoom meeting at 6:30 p.m. and resumed his duties

  Brian Keith, a Lomita resident, spoke in opposition to the project. He urged the Council to vote
  no on the subdivision of the property into three smaller lots.

  Walt (no last name given), a Lomita resident, expressed opposition to the project due to
  inadequate emergency vehicle access, street parking issues, and water runoff problems.

  As there were no further requests from the public to speak on this item, Mayor Waronek closed
  the public hearing at 6:34 p.m. He then recognized a request to speak, and reopened the
  public hearing at 6:35 p.m.

  Denise Mutschke, a Lomita resident, stated that the property has been a nuisance for the past
  few years. She expressed concerns relative to runoff and the resulting possible degrading of
  her property.

  Kevin McMinn, the applicant, stated that a condition of the grading permit is that nothing drains
  into adjacent properties from the site.

  As there were no further requests from the public to speak on this item, Mayor Waronek closed
  the public hearing at 6:51 p.m., and brought the item back to the Council for discussion or a
  motion.

  Council Member Uphoff made a motion, secrnded by Council Member Waite to adopt
  Resolution 2021-28, approving Vesting Tentative Parcel Map No. 83029 to subdivide a 23,200
  square-foot single-family residential lot into three new single-family lots and the corresponding
  CEQA Categorical Exemption, subject to the conditions of approval. ln addition, it was
  specified that the applicant stay on top of the grading requirements and communicate with
  interested neighbors.

  Page 5 of I
 Lomita City Council Adjourned Regular Meeting Minutes
August 3, 2021

  MOTION CARRIED by the following vote:

  AYES: Council Members: Gazeley, Uphoff, Waite, and Mayor Pro Tem Segawa
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: Mayor Waronek (did not vote because he was absent for the staff report)

  Adopted the following titled resolution:

  RESOLUTION NO. 2021-28. A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LOMITA, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING VESTING TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP NO.83029
  FOR THE SUBDIVISION OF 26275 APPIAN WAY INTO THREE LOTS IN THE
  RESTDENTTAL STNGLE-FAM|LY (R-1) ZONE AND FTND|NG THAT THE PROJECT tS
  EXEMPT FROM CEQA REQUIREMENTS. FILED BY KEVIN MCMINN, 30229
  KINGSRIDGE DRIVE, RANCHO PALOS VERDES, CA 90275

10, DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION TO APPROVE VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP
  NO. 78233 - 26016 OAK STREET tN THE RESTDENTIAL VARTABLE DENSTTY (RVD)-2500
  ZONE

  RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution 2021-29, approving Vesting Tentative Tract
  Map No. 78233 for the development of a one-lot condominium subdivision consisting of nine
  residential townhome units on a 23,418 square-foot lot located at 26016 Oak Street in the
  Residential Variable Density (RVD)-2500 zone and the corresponding CEQA Categorical
  Exemption, subject to the conditions of approval.

  Associate Planner MacMorran presented the staff report as per the agenda material.

  Mayor Waronek opened the public hearing at 6:59 p.m.

  Dean Skinner, the applicant, stated that the homeowners' association could include language
  requiring that residents use their garages for parking (rather than for storage, etc.).

  Nancy (no last name given), a Lomita resident, expressed concerns relative to street parking,
  traffic flow, and speeding in the area. She asked about the condition of a section of sidewalk
  nexl to the property.

  Mr. Skinner stated that the sidewalk would be patched in the course of construction.

  lvan Yermakov, a Lomita resident, expressed concems relative to street parking and
  speeding. He asked about landscaping on the property.

  Mr. Skinner stated that landscaping plans have been submitted, and include the addition of
  trees and grassy areas along Oak Street and near the northernmost corner of the property.

  Associate Planner MacMorran added that the proposal includes a lreelined publicly owned
  parkway along the entire site frontage on Oak Street.

  Sebastian Blanco, a Lomita resident, expressed concems relative to street parking. He
  recommended that the project have fewer units and provide more onsite parking. He also
  spoke of speeding and frequent double parking in the area.

  Page 6 of 8
 Lomita City Council Adjourned Regular Meeling Minutes
August 3, 2021

  Mayor Waronek allowed Mr. Yermakov to speak again.

  Mr. Yermakov stated that the project would be more acceptable in his view if there were fewer
  units.

  As there were no further requests from the public to speak on this item, Mayor Waronek closed
  the public hearing at 7:1'1 p.m.

  Associate Planner MacMonan stressed that the project complies with the City's residential
  parking standards.

  As Mayor Waronek recognized another request to speak, he reopened the public hearing at
  7:12p.m.

  Wade Kyle, a Lomita resident, recognized the rights of the builder but asked if he could be
  required to not exacerbate the street parking issues. He also inquired about reformulating the
  City's Code regarding parking. City Manager Smoot stated that the City's upcoming
  discussions regarding the Housing Element and General Plan Update might be an appropriate
  venue for discussions related to the residential parking requirements.

  Council Member Gazeley made a motion, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Segawa to adopt
  Resolution 2021-29, approving Vesting Tentative Tract Map No. 78233 for the development
  of a one-lot condominium subdivision consisting of nine residential townhome units on a
  23,418 square-foot lot located at 26016 Oak Street in the Residential Variable Density (RVD)-
  2500 zone and the conesponding CEQA Categorical Exemption, subject to the conditions of
  approval.

  MOTION CARRIED by the following vote:

  AYES: Council Members: Gazeley, Uphoff, Waite, and Mayor Pro Tem Segawa, and
  Mayor Waronek
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None

  Adopted the following titled resolution:

  RESOLUTION NO. 2021-29 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LOMITA, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP NO.78233 FOR
  A ONE-LOT SUBDIVISION CONSISTING OF NINE RESIDENTIAL CONDOMINIUM
  (TOWNHOME) UNTTS ON A 23,418-SQUARE-FOOT LOT LOCATED AT 26016 OAK
  STREET tN THE RESTDENTTAL VARTABLE DENSTW-2500 (RVD-2500) ZONE AND
  FINDING THAT THE PROJECT IS EXEMPT FROM CEQA REQUIREMENTS. FILE BY
  JEANNA RUBY, ON BEHALF OF E & S PRIME BUILDERS, 1981 ARTESIA BLVD. #8,
  REDONDO BEACH, CA 90278

  Page 7 of 8
 Lomita City Council Adjourned Regular Meeting Minutes
August 3, 2021

11. ADJOURNMENT

  There being no further business to discuss, Mayor Waronek adjourned the meeting, in
  memory of Martin Nakazawa and Brenda Klee, at 7:17 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,

  Linda  Abbott, Deputy City Clerk
